title: Memory or a Clock? Auditing a Memory Advantage in XLand-MiniGrid with Seeds, Maps and Evaluation Noise Apart
abstract: arXiv:2610.33816v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: On a partially observable XLand-MiniGrid task, an LSTM agent beats a memory-free MLP by 25 percentage points. The gap looks like a clear case of memory. We ask two questions about it. First, how much of a measured gap is noise? Separating training seed, map and evaluation randomness in 60 runs, each re-evaluated three times, we find that about ten paired seeds detect a 10-point gap in final success. The binary "task acquired" verdict, a common summary of learning curves, is 76% evaluation noise and would need about a hundred seeds for the same gap. Second, is the gap memory? On a sealed panel of new maps, opened once, a memory-free MLP of the LSTM's size comes within 3.3 points of the LSTM when it is given the time step, and gains no measurable benefit from its width without it. With the time step, an MLP a quarter of the LSTM's size, and the LSTM with its state erased at every step, also come within about 5 points. A linear probe read

translated_title: 记忆还是时钟？通过分离种子、地图与评估噪声审计XLand-MiniGrid中的记忆优势
translated_abstract: 在部分可观测的XLand-MiniGrid任务上，LSTM智能体比无记忆的MLP高出25个百分点，这一差距看似是记忆能力带来优势的明确例证。我们对此提出两个问题。第一，测量到的差距中有多少是噪声？通过在60次运行中分离训练种子、地图和评估随机性（每次运行重新评估三次），我们发现大约十个配对种子即可检测到最终成功率中10个百分点的差距；而作为学习曲线常见总结指标的二元“任务习得”判定，其中76%是评估噪声，对同样的差距需要约一百个种子才能可靠检测。第二，这个差距真的是记忆吗？在一个一次性开启的全新地图密封测试集上，与LSTM同等规模的无记忆MLP在被提供时间步信息时，与LSTM的差距缩小到3.3个百分点以内；而在没有时间步信息时，单纯增大其宽度并不能带来可测量的收益。在提供时间步的情况下，一个规模仅为LSTM四分之一的MLP，以及在每一步都将其状态清零的LSTM，也都能将差距缩小到约5个百分点以内。线性探针读取……
tldr: 该论文通过分离种子、地图与评估噪声进行严格统计审计，发现XLand-MiniGrid上LSTM相对无记忆MLP的25个百分点“记忆优势”大半可归因于时间步信息——给定时间步后，规模仅四分之一的无记忆MLP即可将差距缩小到约3-5个百分点，同时揭示二元“任务习得”判定中76%实为评估噪声。
en_tdlr: Through a rigorous audit separating seeds, maps and evaluation noise, this paper shows that the LSTM's 25-point "memory advantage" over memory-free MLPs on XLand-MiniGrid largely reduces to a time-step cue—with the time step given, a memory-free MLP a quarter of the LSTM's size narrows the gap to about 3-5 points—and that the binary "task acquired" verdict is 76% evaluation noise.
